test_goal.title: Test target
test_goal.body: The FermatMind Enneagram test offers hypotheses about motivational structure that you can read, observe, and provide feedback on. It first shows the primary candidate, top three candidates, full nine-type profile, and close-candidate comparison, then brings the reading back to real situations. This technical note explains how response signals and interpretation rules generate these modules, and which parts remain theoretical interpretations or product hypotheses.

e105_fc144_forms.title: E105 and FC144 two forms
e105_fc144_forms.body: The E105 five-point rating form uses intensity ratings to build a full nine-type profile and top three candidates. The FC144 two-option forced-choice form records relative trade-off signals through paired choices. The forms have the same evidence level, but their score sources and the questions they address differ. FC144 does not override E105's primary candidate.

score_space_boundary.title: Score space boundary
score_space_boundary.body: E105 scores come from five-point intensity ratings; FC144 scores come from relative preferences in paired choices. They can use the same result structure, but they do not support the same numerical comparison.

dominance_gap.title: Dominance Gap
dominance_gap.body: The leading-candidate gap describes the relative distance between the first and second candidates within the same form and score space. It guides the tone used for a clear pattern, close-candidate comparison, or a diffuse distribution. E105 and FC144 use different scoring units, so this gap is not a common yardstick across forms, populations, or time. It is also not a measurement-error range, statistical confidence interval, norm-based rank, proof of external validity, or certainty about personality.

confidence_band.title: Interpretation stability
confidence_band.body: Interpretation stability controls the result page's tone, module visibility, and suggested actions. A clear pattern means the interpretation is relatively concentrated within this form on this occasion; close-candidate comparison calls for reading candidates side by side; a diffuse distribution calls for less certainty about a single number; and a response-quality boundary means the signals do not support a strong interpretation.

close_call.title: Close-call
close_call.body: When the first and second candidates are close, the page offers a side-by-side comparison and a 7-day observation task, rather than turning a small gap into a definite conclusion.

diffuse.title: Diffuse
diffuse.body: A diffuse distribution means several type signals appear together, and the first candidate and neighboring candidates do not yet support a strong primary-candidate narrative. The page shifts attention to shared themes among the top three candidates, the three-center distribution, recent counterexamples, and observation tasks that can be reviewed.

low_quality.title: Response-quality limits
low_quality.body: When quality signals are triggered, the page narrows its interpretive tone and suggests retaking the same form when your state is stable, rather than labeling you.

retake_stability.title: Retake Stability
retake_stability.body: This technical note will continue tracking retest stability, but it does not promise a stability rate until evidence about samples, time intervals, and response quality is sufficient. Analysis must distinguish same-form retests, agreement across forms, short-term changes in state, and user feedback. A difference in one retest cannot be interpreted as personality change.

e105_fc144_agreement.title: E105 / FC144 Agreement
e105_fc144_agreement.body: Agreement between E105 and FC144 describes overlap in the first or top three candidates across the two forms. It does not mean their scores can be compared directly. It describes agreement in candidate ranking only and cannot, on its own, establish the Enneagram model's external validity, clinical validity, or ability to predict career outcomes.

resonance_feedback.title: Resonance Feedback
resonance_feedback.body: Users' day-7 resonance feedback and self-confirmed types enter history as self-observation evidence for research and content calibration, without silently overriding the primary candidate. Feedback is an observation layer, not a system reclassification. It can indicate which narratives need less weight, additional counterexamples, or revised wording, but a sense of resonance cannot be equated directly with measurement correctness.

method_boundaries.title: method boundaries
method_boundaries.body: This test supports understanding personality patterns and self-observation. It is not for clinical diagnosis, hiring screening, treatment advice, health-level judgments, or fixed personality conclusions. The current version retains wings, arrows, subtypes, and developmental stages only as theoretical background or placeholders for future modules, without hard judgments. This technical note distinguishes product rules, operational metrics being collected, planned stability metrics, and theoretical interpretation frameworks; it does not present them with the same degree of certainty.

privacy.title: Privacy and data
privacy.body: Public explanations use aggregated method metrics only. They do not disclose individual answers, private observation text, or feedback records that identify a user. Shared pages do not show private observations by default, and a user's confirmed type is not treated as the system's final type. Feedback, sample content, and technical metrics follow minimum-necessary use, aggregated display, and traceability. Metrics still being planned or collected show definitions and collection directions, without invented figures.

e105_standard_methodology.label: E105 rating method
e105_standard_methodology.copy: The E105 five-point Likert form uses rating responses to form a full nine-type profile, top three candidates, a leading-candidate gap, and close-call comparison within one scoring context. It is a starting point for self-observation, and its scores are interpreted only within E105.

fc144_forced_choice_methodology.label: FC144 paired-choice method
fc144_forced_choice_methodology.copy: The FC144 two-option forced-choice form records relative motivational signals in difficult trade-offs through paired choices. It can serve as another observation after close-candidate comparison. The forms have the same evidence level. FC144 does not replace E105's primary candidate, top three candidates, or original scoring facts. Read results within FC144's own form boundaries; differences across forms cannot be interpreted as personality change or a judgment that one assessment is better.

same_model_not_same_score_space.label: One model, separate score spaces
same_model_not_same_score_space.copy: E105 and FC144 share an Enneagram interpretation framework, but their forms, response tasks, scoring sources, and error structures differ. They do not share a score space. Result pages may reuse structure and safety boundaries; history, sharing, PDF, and retest entry points must retain each form's provenance. The page does not directly compare their numerical values or interpret differences in the top three candidates across forms as changes in individual state, personality development, or evidence that one is more true.

cross_form_compare_blocked.label: Cross-form comparison limits
cross_form_compare_blocked.copy: Cross-form comparison is disabled. Unless a validated equivalence mapping becomes available, E105 and FC144 remain in separate scoring contexts, and history, sharing, and result-review surfaces do not infer improvement, decline, health status, or measurement precision from their differences.

non_diagnostic_boundary.label: Non-diagnostic use
non_diagnostic_boundary.copy: This result is only for understanding personality patterns, self-observation, and reflective dialogue. Current research is insufficient to treat the Enneagram as a fully validated clinical scale. It is not for mental-health judgments, treatment advice, hiring screening, job matching, ability evaluation, or individual risk assessment. High scores, the primary candidate, top three candidates, close-candidate comparison, diffuse distributions, and response-quality notices are interpretation hypotheses that must be checked against real situations.

user_confirmed_type_boundary.label: Self-observation feedback
user_confirmed_type_boundary.copy: A user's confirmed type records evidence of their own resonance after observation. It is not a system reclassification or external confirmation. It may enter history to mark the user's perspective for later reading. Sharing and result review show it only as a self-observation note, without overriding the primary candidate, top three candidates, scorer output, or scoring facts from the original responses.

low_quality_boundary.label: Response-quality limits
low_quality_boundary.copy: When response-quality signals are triggered, the result remains readable, but its interpretation boundaries narrow substantially. The page retains only light observation suggestions and avoids turning a single set of responses into a definite type judgment. It first suggests retaking the same form when your state is stable and you have enough time. Switching forms offers another observation only; it cannot bypass quality limits, seek an ideal answer, prove personality change, or compare score increases and decreases.

diffuse_boundary.label: Diffuse-profile interpretation
diffuse_boundary.copy: Diffuse means the nine type signals do not yet form a clear leading pattern. The page lowers certainty about any one number and prioritizes the top three candidates, center distribution, recent counterexamples, and a seven-day observation task. Retesting provides another response sample; it does not automatically correct the result to a particular type.

close_call_boundary.label: Close-candidate interpretation
close_call_boundary.copy: A close-call means the first and second candidates are close. The page turns their differences into side-by-side comparison, counterexample checks, and seven-day observation questions without requiring a forced type decision.

disclaimers.label: Not diagnostic
disclaimers.copy: This test supports personality-pattern reflection and is not for clinical diagnosis or treatment advice.

disclaimers.label: No clinical-validity claim
disclaimers.copy: This version makes no claim of external clinical validity, accuracy, or predictive ability.

disclaimers.label: Not for hiring
disclaimers.copy: This test is not for hiring, promotion, termination, or employment screening.

disclaimers.label: No hard theory judgment
disclaimers.copy: Wing, arrow, subtype, and health level are not hard system conclusions in this version.

disclaimers.label: No cross-form numeric comparison
disclaimers.copy: E105 and FC144 share one model but use different scoring spaces and are not compared numerically by default.

disclaimers.label: Self-observation boundary
disclaimers.copy: The type a user recognizes after observation records personal reflection. It never silently overwrites the measured leading candidate.
